title: Timing in seconds, minutes and hours
keyIdea: We measure how long something takes in seconds, minutes or hours. Seconds are short, like a blink. Minutes are longer, like brushing your teeth. Hours are longest, like a night of sleep. 60 seconds make 1 minute. A stopwatch counts the seconds while something happens, and a sand timer shows when a set time is up. When we write it down, we say how long it took, such as 'about 2 minutes', not a time of day like '2 o'clock'.
familyTip: Time some everyday jobs together with a phone stopwatch or a kitchen timer: putting on shoes, tidying the toys, a bath. Before you start, guess: seconds or minutes? Then say the result out loud, such as 'That took about 3 minutes'.

visual.caption: Seconds, minutes or hours? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort jobs by unit, fill a 1-minute sand timer 10 seconds at a time, time a frog with a stopwatch, write times down, brush for 2 minutes.

kid: Some things take a short time and some take a long time. We use units to say how long. A second is very short. A blink takes about a second. A minute is longer. Brushing your teeth takes about 2 minutes. An hour is longer still. A night of sleep takes many hours.
60 seconds make 1 minute. You can count to 60 in tens: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. That is 6 tens. It is not 100. A sand timer that lasts 1 minute holds 60 seconds of sand.
A stopwatch counts the seconds. Press Start when the job starts. Press Stop when the job ends. Then read the number. If it says 8, the job took 8 seconds.
When you write it down, say how long it took and add the unit: 8 seconds, 2 minutes, 3 hours. Do not write 2 o'clock. O'clock tells you when something happens, not how long it takes.
adult: Ages 5 to 6. This matches the National Curriculum in England for Year 1 Measurement: measure and begin to record time (hours, minutes, seconds), and compare, describe and solve practical problems for time. It links to CCSS K.MD.A.1 and K.MD.A.2 (describe and compare measurable attributes) and leads into Year 2 work on minutes in an hour. Key words: time, duration, second, minute, hour, stopwatch, sand timer, longer, shorter, how long.

The aim at this stage is a feel for the size of each unit and the habit of recording a duration with a number and a unit. Children should know that 1 minute is 60 seconds, but they are not yet expected to convert between units or read a clock to the minute. Sand timers are a good first tool because the whole minute is visible, and a stopwatch shows seconds counting up in real time.

Common mistakes: thinking a minute is 100 seconds, because they count in hundreds elsewhere; choosing a unit that is far too short or too long, such as 'brushing teeth takes 2 hours'; stopping a stopwatch early or late, so the reading is not how long the job took; and mixing up a duration with a time of day, as in 'my swim took 3 o'clock'. The lab, practice and challenge each target these slips.

In the lab your child sorts six everyday jobs into seconds, minutes and hours, fills a 1-minute sand timer with scoops of 10 seconds until it is full at 60, times a frog's hops with a stopwatch and must press Stop as it lands, picks the right words to record three timings, and turns a 1-minute sand timer twice to brush for 2 minutes. The sand in the last step is sped up and says so.

practice.prompt: Which unit would you use to time a blink?
practice.hint: A blink is over very fast. Which unit is the shortest?
practice.explain: A blink takes about a second, so we time it in seconds, the shortest unit.

practice.prompt: A 1-minute sand timer runs out {n} times while you tidy your room. How many minutes did you tidy?
practice.hint: Each time the sand runs out, 1 minute has gone by. Count the turns.
practice.explain: {n} turns of a 1-minute timer is {n} minutes of tidying.

practice.prompt: Each scoop of sand is 10 seconds. You put {n} scoops in the timer. How many seconds is that?
practice.hint: Count in tens, one ten for each scoop: 10, 20, 30 …

practice.prompt: A stopwatch shows 7 when the race ends. How long did the race take?
practice.hint: A stopwatch counts seconds. Is o'clock a time of day or a length of time?
practice.explain: The stopwatch counted 7 seconds, so the race took 7 seconds. O'clock is a time of day.

practice.prompt: Which of these takes the longest time?
practice.hint: Which one lasts hours? Which lasts minutes? Which lasts a second?
practice.explain: A school day lasts hours, brushing teeth takes minutes and a clap takes about a second.

pool.hint: Count the 10-second scoops that fill a 1-minute timer.
pool.explain: 6 scoops of 10 seconds fill the timer, so 60 seconds make 1 minute, not 100.

pool.prompt: A 1-minute timer has {=10*n} seconds of sand in it so far. How many more seconds of sand will fill it?
pool.hint: A full minute is 60 seconds. Count on in tens from {=10*n} to 60.
pool.explain: {=10*n} seconds and {=60-10*n} more seconds make 60 seconds, which is 1 minute.

pool.prompt: Which unit fits eating a snack?
pool.hint: A snack is longer than a blink but much shorter than a night of sleep.
pool.explain: Eating a snack takes a few minutes: longer than seconds, shorter than hours.

pool.prompt: When should you stop the stopwatch?
pool.hint: You want the stopwatch to show how long the whole job took.
pool.explain: Stop it when the job ends. Then the number shows how long the job took.

pool.prompt: Sam turns a 1-minute sand timer {n} times while he reads. Then he turns it 1 more time. How many minutes did he read?
pool.hint: Each turn is 1 minute. Count all the turns, then add the last one.
pool.explain: {n} turns and 1 more is {=n+1} turns, so Sam read for {=n+1} minutes.

pool.hint: You press Start when a job begins and Stop when it ends.
pool.explain: A stopwatch measures how long something takes, by counting the seconds.

pool.prompt: Tom says, 'My swim took 3 o'clock.' What is wrong?
choices: O'clock tells when, not how long
pool.hint: Is 3 o'clock a length of time, or a time on the clock?
pool.explain: 3 o'clock is when something happens. To say how long, Tom needs seconds, minutes or hours.

pool.prompt: Which is longer, 1 minute or 1 second?
pool.hint: How many seconds fit in 1 minute?
pool.explain: 1 minute is longer. It is 60 seconds, so 60 seconds fit inside it.

pool.prompt: Which would you time in hours?
pool.hint: Hours are for long things. Which one lasts a long time?
pool.explain: A long car trip lasts hours. A sneeze takes a second and a sock takes seconds.
